trust_decision.summary: main() decides, once and process-wide, which directories the PATH environment variable may contain before libarchive spawns external filter programs (gpg, base64, brotli, lzop, compress, grzip, and libarchive's own fallbacks) via PATH lookup; -o noexternal is supposed to make that lookup fail entirely.

landing_point.why: The only PATH write in the project; a 'PATH hijacking' summary leads straight to the setenv("PATH", ...) in main().

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI: fuse-archive <archive> [mount_point] (default, external filters allowed) -> new SetSafePath() filters inherited PATH to an allow-list
CLI: fuse-archive -o noexternal ... -> PATH set to /dev/null instead of empty string (empty PATH element = current directory)
CLI: -o unsafe_path option (new opt-out keeping original PATH; ignored with noexternal)
CLI: shared safe_empty_path constant used by SetSafePath and noexternal branch

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changes are in fuse-archive.cc main(); the spawn sink is inside libarchive (archive_read_append_filter_program at lib/reader.cc:528 and archive_read_support_filter_all at lib/reader.cc:640, lib/reader.cc:836), which inherits the process environment, so the one global setenv covers it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue that -o noexternal with PATH="" already 'clears' PATH, so the empty-string-means-current-directory behaviour of execvp is a libc quirk outside the project (noexternal branch, fuse-archive.cc:372).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: By default, external filters in system dirs must keep working (romeo.txt.b64 must mount via /usr/bin/base64). -o unsafe_path must keep the user's PATH, and noexternal must win over unsafe_path. Forcing PATH to empty or /dev/null for everyone breaks default .b64/.gpg/.br mounts.

O6_input_shapes: inherited PATH containing an attacker-controlled directory before the system dirs
PATH entries with trailing slashes ('/usr/bin/') normalised by Path::WithoutTrailingSeparator (lib/path.cc:31-40)
empty PATH elements / PATH empty (current directory in execvp), handled by never emitting empty and falling back to /dev/null

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A filter command built with an absolute or user-configurable program path (e.g. an '-o gpg=PROG' style option) that bypasses PATH sanitisation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SET_FILTER_COMMAND already builds command strings for external programs; a maintainer adding configurability for gpg/brotli locations would plausibly add an option here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A code path that runs before PATH sanitisation at fuse-archive.cc:365 (the --help/--version branches already call fuse_main early) and spawns a helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Early-exit branches precede the sanitisation; a new early helper call (e.g. printing external tool versions in --version) would naturally land there.

O9_family: CWE-426 untrusted search path (environment-based program lookup)

O10_build.toolchain: make + g++/clang, pkg-config, libfuse (2 or 3) dev headers, libarchive dev headers
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test.py (TestPathSanitization at tests/test.py:2270-2301, run via Makefile 'check' target at Makefile:134); the tests actually mount through FUSE, so they need /dev/fuse and fusermount

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep the fixed hard-coded safe PATH (already at pinned) or setenv("PATH", "") for everyone, without noticing that an empty PATH means the current directory, and without adding the unsafe_path opt-out.

out_of_scope_notes: gpg is spawned with the full inherited environment (GNUPGHOME etc.), so it loads its own helpers and config; this is outside the PATH protection.
libfuse may fall back to a PATH lookup for fusermount after the PATH change; this is in an external library and was not pursued.
unverified: Fix commit 4b13a49 is already in the pinned tree: fuse-archive.cc:365-372 and tests/test.py:2270-2301 match its post-image. The real remaining delta is therefore 6f086e6 only (allow-list filter, /dev/null for noexternal, -o unsafe_path). I did not confirm the ancestry with git.
The claim that glibc execvp treats PATH="" as the current directory is from libc behaviour, not from repo code.

Whether libarchive's built-in fallbacks (lz4/zstd/lzop/lrzip external commands, reached via SET_FILTER and support_filter_all) spawn through PATH depends on how libarchive was built; this is not in the repo. All of them inherit the one global PATH anyway.
repo_mb not measured; the source is a handful of .cc/.h files (well under 5 MB), but the test data is binary.
needs_gpu_kernel_gui is flagged because behavioural tests mount via FUSE (kernel module /dev/fuse). The PATH logic itself could be tested without mounting only through a harness we add.
present_in_latest is not applicable: there are no O8 routes and no latest release was given.
